description: Python project conventions. Everything lands under dev- (which is what bump-version keys on) unless a later rule says otherwise; test/lint/build tooling is grouped, automerged, and never cuts a release.

packageRules.description: Base. Every pep621/dockerfile update lands under the dev- branch prefix. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: each repo's bump-version job gates on $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_SOURCE_BRANCH_NAME =~ /^renovate\/dev-/, so the prefix is what decides whether an update bumps VERSION, writes a changelog fragment, and cuts a release. Rules below override it for updates that must not do that.

Low-churn runtime libraries — batch the ones that move often and carry little behaviour. A positive list rather than a catch-all on purpose: a catch-all here would override the `cloud sdks` groupName set by the default preset, since preset rules are applied before this file's. Deliberately excluded and left one-per-MR: sqlalchemy and alembic (ORM and migration tooling against a live database), plus yt-dlp, discord.py, redis, pydantic, davey, spotipy, ytmusicapi, moviepy, asyncpg and aiohttp — the deps where a bad bump is a production incident and you want a single commit to revert.

Test, lint and build tooling. Grouped, automerged, and never cuts a release because the test- prefix keeps bump-version from firing. Two changes from the previous version of this rule. First, globs instead of thirteen exact names: that list had drifted past what the repos actually declare, so pytest-postgresql, psycopg[binary] and setuptools were falling through to the dev- prefix and cutting production releases for test-only dependencies — renovate/dev-setuptools-84.x merged into discord-bot on 2026-08-10 and did exactly that, and enheduanna carries setuptools in its test extra too. Second, this rule is now listed LAST and overrides the dev- base rule above, which removes the negated copy of this same list the old config had to carry. That duplication was the reason the drift went unnoticed: adding a dep meant editing two places and forgetting the second failed silently. Note majors are included, so a major pylint or tox bump still automerges behind a green pipeline — unchanged from the previous behaviour; add matchUpdateTypes if you want those reviewed.
